mcp.title: Add an MCP server
mcp.desc: Add an MCP server manually: the config is written to ~/.meowcode/mcp.json and connects automatically after saving.
mcp.envHint: Supports ${VAR} references to MeowCode process environment variables.
mcp.jsonHint: Accepts a {"mcpServers": {…}} wrapper (adds several at once) or a bare server object.
mcp.jsonIdInvalid: Invalid id "{{id}}": must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen.

mcp.headersInvalid: Headers are not a valid JSON object.

delete.desc: This forks the repository, creates a delete branch, removes the entry folder and opens a delete PR. The entry is only really gone once the PR is reviewed and merged; your local copy stays installed.
delete.title: Delete the community entry “{{name}}”?

body.deletePrCreated: Delete PR created, waiting for the repository owner to review and merge it.

disconnect.desc: This deletes the {{platform}} token stored on this machine and disconnects the {{platform}} MCP right away.
disconnect.envHint: To revoke the token completely, delete it in the access token settings of that platform.
disconnect.platformHint: The authorization record on the platform is not revoked automatically; to revoke it, remove MeowCode from {{platform}} settings → Authorized apps.
disconnect.title: Disconnect {{platform}}

pluginConfirm.desc: Community plugins are TypeScript source. Once installed they run directly inside your MeowCode agent process, with the same permissions as official plugins (reading and writing files, running commands, and so on). MeowCode does not sandbox community plugins.
pluginConfirm.title: Install the community plugin “{{name}}”?

github.connected: GitHub is connected. Loading GitHub MCP tools.
github.desc: Authorize MeowCode through the GitHub OAuth device flow. The token is encrypted and stored on this machine, and is only used for GitHub MCP.
github.deviceFlowStep: In your <0>GitHub App settings</0>, turn on Enable device flow
github.moduleMissing: The GitHub sign-in module is not loaded yet. Restart MeowCode completely and try again.
github.permissions: Grant repository permissions such as Contents, Issues, Pull requests and Actions as needed
github.prereq: Before authorizing, make sure the GitHub App has:
github.title: Connect GitHub
github.waiting: Waiting for you to authorize on GitHub… the device code is valid for {{count}} minute
github.waiting_one: Waiting for you to authorize on GitHub… the device code is valid for {{count}} minute
github.waiting_other: Waiting for you to authorize on GitHub… the device code is valid for {{count}} minutes

oauth.awaitingBrowser: Waiting for authorization in the browser…
oauth.awaitingUser: Waiting for you to finish authorizing in the browser…
oauth.clientIdHint: This is the Client ID of the app built into MeowCode. If you use your own app, change both this and the Secret below to the values on the app page — a mismatched pair fails the token exchange (401).
oauth.clientIdLabel: Client ID (must belong to the same app as the Client Secret below)
oauth.clientIdPlaceholder: Client ID of the OAuth app
oauth.connectHint: “Connect now” opens the {{platform}} authorization page in your system browser and redirects back to this machine afterwards — no token pasting needed.
oauth.desc: Authorize directly with {{platform}} OAuth: clicking the button opens the authorization page in your system browser and returns to MeowCode when you are done. Credentials stay on this machine and are only used to connect {{platform}} MCP.
oauth.directTitle: Connect directly: authorize {{platform}} in the browser, no token pasting
oauth.moduleMissing: The OAuth module is not loaded yet. Restart MeowCode and try again.
oauth.redirectLabel: Callback URL (must match the one registered for your {{platform}} OAuth app)
oauth.requireClientId: Enter the Client ID (it must belong to the same app as the Client Secret).
oauth.requireToken: Fill in at least one token.
oauth.secretFilePath: You can also keep the Secret in %APPDATA%\MeowCode\oauth-apps.json (never committed)
oauth.secretLabel: Client Secret ({{platform}} requires it for the token exchange; fill it in once)
oauth.secretPlaceholder: Client Secret of the OAuth app
oauth.setupHint: You only see this form once: {{platform}} requires a Client Secret for the token exchange (the platform does not support PKCE), so it is filled in on the first run and encrypted on this machine. “Save and connect” opens the browser straight away; from then on every “Connect {{platform}}” goes straight to the browser without this form.
oauth.usePat: Use a personal access token instead

manualToken.desc: The token is encrypted and stored on this machine and used to connect {{name}}. It is validated online before saving, then the server reconnects and loads its tools.
manualToken.hintFigma: Create one in the Figma website under Settings → Security → Personal access tokens; read access to File content is enough.
manualToken.hintLuckin: Sign in at open.lkcoffee.com/mcp to create and copy a Token; used by the Luckin coffee-ordering MCP (order, track, pickup code).
manualToken.title: Set the {{name}} access token
